The female counterpart of the English di.why: 'Quarbel' is a made-up English dialect noun, not a word of standard English. A regional word for a role could have a female counterpart without the record knowing of it, and nothing in the record gives 'quarbel' a counterpart already. As a dialect noun it may share a counterpart with a standard noun (a regional synonym of 'brother' sharing 'sister'), so 'sister' keeping 'brother' as its standard counterpart is not overwritten.

notes: ABox expansion paired with grammar-replace-0003 (husband -> sister). Keeps relation gender_counterpart_of and the new object 'sister' with a made-up English dialect noun 'quarbel'. The first version used a plain noun, which put 'sister' (already the counterpart of 'brother') under a second counterpart and so overwrote a filled slot; a dialect noun is exempt from 'functional' in RELATIONS.md (a regional synonym may share a counterpart), the same way as in grammar-insert-d001, so the pairing reads as a regional word for 'brother' sharing 'sister'. Under symmetry the insert also makes 'quarbel' a male counterpart of 'sister' next to 'brother'. Derived questions: plural, the shared counterpart with 'brother', letter count. Near and far queries are copied from the revision.
